import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 94

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/94](https://www.erdosproblems.com/94)
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka
  (1992), 44-48.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I
  (1997), 47-67.
- [LeTh95] Lefmann, Hanno and Thiele, Torsten, *Point sets with distinct distances*. Combinatorica
  (1995), 379-408.
-/

open Filter EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos94

/-- The regular $n$-gon inscribed in the unit circle. -/
noncomputable def regularNGon (n : ℕ) : Finset ℝ² :=
  (Finset.range n).image fun k : ℕ =>
    !₂[Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * k / n), Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * k / n)]

/--
Suppose $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ determine a convex polygon and the set of distances between
them is $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose $u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of
points. Then
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3.$$

In [Er97c] Erdős claims that Fishburn solved this, but gives no reference.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos94.lean"]
theorem erdos_94 : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ², ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Note it is trivial that $\sum f(u_i)=\binom{n}{2}$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_94.variants.sum_multiplicity (P : Finset ℝ²) :
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, distanceMultiplicity P u = P.card.choose 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Lefmann and Theile [LeTh95] prove a stronger version of this question, that
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3$$
under the weaker assumption that no three points are on a line.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_94.variants.no_three_on_a_line : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    NonTrilinear (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Fishburn also make the stronger conjecture that $\sum f(u_i)^2$ is maximal for the
regular $n$-gon (for large enough $n$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    P.card = n → ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ u ∈ distanceSet (regularNGon n), (distanceMultiplicity (regularNGon n) u : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos94

reformulations.difference: The Lean formulation requires one positive constant for all finite point sets in convex position, including sets with fewer than three points, rather than stating an asymptotic bound for n-vertex convex polygons.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 3, ConvexIndep expresses that the points are precisely vertices of their convex hull. The extra cases are harmless: the energy is zero for n = 0 or 1 and is one for n = 2. More generally, any finitely many exceptional sizes in an asymptotic formulation can be absorbed into a uniform constant: the multiplicities are nonnegative and sum to choose(n,2), so their squared sum is at most choose(n,2)^2, independently of the configuration. The global bound conversely implies the asymptotic bound immediately.

could_not_verify: Erdos94.erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon: The construction and comparison quantity were verified, but the precise range of n and current open status could not be settled against the cited webpage. Requests to https://www.erdosproblems.com/94 returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The accessible Lefmann–Thiele preprint, pp. 18–19, records the sharper conjectures for every odd n ≥ 3 and every even n ≥ 10; these ranges are stronger than an unspecified eventual threshold. I could not verify whether the webpage itself poses the eventual version used here. The full Er92e and Er97c texts were also unavailable. I therefore do not report the threshold difference as a confirmed defect.
review.notes: Checked all five declarations and the underlying Euclidean-space notation, distanceSet, distanceMultiplicity, ConvexIndep, NonTrilinear, and Triplewise definitions. Scratch proofs verify empty/singleton/two-point cases, exclusion of distance zero, exact division by two in the multiplicity, the sum_multiplicity identity, regularNGon n having exactly n vertices for every n, and all its vertices lying on the unit circle. The external proof's relevant theorems kernel-check with only standard axioms after two transparency-related compatibility edits in the scratch copy for Lean 4.33.1; its explicit 3/4 bound supplies a uniform constant, despite its separate pointwise Big-O wrapper. The solved statuses of the cubic bounds are supported by Lefmann–Thiele. No checkout files were edited. Source-access limitations below prevent an unconditional certification of the entire file.
